children: Karyopharm Therapeutics filed for bankruptcy, planning to merge with Ayrmid Ltd. and to continue ordinary operations.
Shares were recently down 84% to 11 cents.

The cancer-focused drug company said it entered a restructuring support agreement with existing lenders and noteholders and other key stakeholders. Existing secured lenders agreed to provide up to $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing, it said.
Ayrmid will be lead bidder in a court-supervised sale process.

Karyopharm said in September that absent additional funding or one or more strategic transactions to extend its cash runway beyond Oct. 15, the company "will be unable to continue as a going concern and may have to consider seeking protection under the bankruptcy laws, liquidating assets or ceasing operations."
Ayrmid is the parent of cell-therapy company Gamida Cell Inc.
